test_title: SSC CPO Tier-II Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8th November 2021)
subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Fair-weather friend

options.text: A person who is not a friend, only an acquaintance
A person whose friendship cannot be relied on in difficult times
A person who is a friend in all good and bad times
A person who is a friend in all your difficulties

solution:
The correct answer is- 'A person whose friendship cannot be relied on in difficult times.' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The meaning of the given idiom is:
 
 
• A fair-weather friend means *someone who is a friend only when things are going right and leaves you when you face trouble*. (कोई है जो केवल तभी दोस्त होता है जब चीजें सही चल रही होती हैं और जब आप परेशानी का सामना करते हैं तो आपको छोड़ देते हैं)

 
 
• Example: *Simran is looking for a loyal friend, not **a fair-weather friend***.
 
 
 
 
 
• By the above meaning and example, we can say that 'A person whose friendship cannot be relied on in difficult times' is the correct answer.

Hence *option 2 *is the appropriate answer. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's learn about the origin of the given idiom:
 
 
• This idiom is used since at least the mid-**1800s**. Though its origin is not available, it can be understood through a story. **Fair-weather **refers to **mild weather**, so the idiom refers to a friend who can be relied upon when the weather is good but abandons you when the weather turns stormy.
